content_types.name: Beginner guide
content_types.purpose: Explain a subject from the ground up and define essential terms.

content_types.name: Step-by-step tutorial
content_types.purpose: Show a reproducible sequence, what the reader should see, and how to confirm success.

content_types.name: Practical project
content_types.purpose: Help the reader build or complete a concrete deliverable with inputs, steps, and an example result.

content_types.name: Formula or calculation tutorial
content_types.purpose: Show exact inputs, formulas, cell references, calculated outputs, and an independent check.

content_types.name: Troubleshooting guide
content_types.purpose: Identify symptoms, likely causes, safe diagnostic steps, and a verifiable resolution.

content_types.name: Comparison
content_types.purpose: Compare options using consistent criteria, current evidence, limitations, and reader-fit recommendations.

content_types.name: Review or evaluation
content_types.purpose: Assess a product or service transparently without pretending to have performed hands-on testing.

content_types.name: Explainer
content_types.purpose: Explain how something works, why it matters, and its limitations.

content_types.name: Checklist or template
content_types.purpose: Provide the complete promised checklist or usable template, not merely describe one.

AI and AI Tools: Distinguish model capabilities from app features and account-plan limits.
Do not present generated answers as verified facts; include a practical fact-checking step.
Check current privacy, data-use, regional availability, and free-versus-paid details when relevant.
Office Software and Everyday Productivit: Name the specific application, platform, and interface path when giving instructions.
Do not assume Word, Google Docs, PowerPoint, and Google Slides have identical features.
For tutorials, state the expected result and an easy way to verify it.
Spreadsheets, Data and Reporting: For formula tutorials, provide a small, complete sample dataset with cell locations.
Show the exact formula, the cell where it belongs, and the expected calculated result.
Recalculate examples independently; check references, ranges, criteria, blanks, and edge cases.
Distinguish Excel-specific features from Google Sheets features and note version or locale differences where relevant.
Never leave a formula as an unevaluated result when the article promises a worked example.
Graphic Design, Video and Content Creati: Distinguish genuine product screenshots from illustrative artwork.
State relevant export dimensions, aspect ratios, file formats, and platform constraints accurately.
Explain licensing and usage rights for fonts, stock assets, music, and generated media when relevant.
Freelancing and Remote Work: Label invented client examples as hypothetical and keep scope, deliverables, timelines, and figures consistent.
Treat rates, deposits, milestones, and payment arrangements as negotiable rather than universal.
Verify country support and withdrawal conditions before recommending a payment service.
Digital Business, Marketing and E-commer: Distinguish platform capabilities, plan limits, fees, and eligibility requirements.
Explain affiliate disclosures and avoid guaranteed income, traffic, or conversion claims.
Verify payment, checkout, and payout availability for the reader's country before making regional claims.
Digital Learning, Research and Study Ski: Distinguish learning support from doing assessed work dishonestly.
Show readers how to evaluate source credibility and verify AI-generated research.
Do not invent citations, academic references, quotations, or research findings.
Digital Foundations, Online Safety and T: Give safe, reversible diagnostic steps before destructive actions such as resets or deletion.
Describe symptoms, likely causes, exact steps, and the expected result.
Never ask readers to expose passwords, recovery codes, private keys, or sensitive account details.
